summary: David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. Gray served as a Woodrow Wilson postdoctoral fellow at Rice University and taught at Santa Clara University.

David Bubna-Litic earned his PhD from Western Sydney University (attested 2000). He held a post as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000), working in Buddhist studies and other fields.

David Burton specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997) and served as Senior Lecturer in Theology and Religious Studies at Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Drewes works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Lawrence University, UW–Madison, and the University of Virginia (PhD 2006 under Karen C. Lang). He held posts at Virginia, Indiana University (2006), and the University of Manitoba (2009–2010).
David E. Cooper (born 1942) is a philosopher who attended Highgate School (~1955–1960). He served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University from 1986 to 2009.

David E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at UCLA, taught at UCSB, UIUC, and the University of Hawaii, and held research posts at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2006) and Oberlin College (2010).
David Faure (born 1947) is a historian and sinologist. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1965–1969) and completed his studies at Princeton University (~1970–1976).

David Fiordalis specializes in Buddhist, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (PhD attested 2008 under Luis Oscar Gómez), he became associate professor and department chair at Linfield University (attested 2017).

David Friedman (1903–1984) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS University of London and Professor at the University of London from ~1950 to ~1970.

David Germano specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992 and served as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia (attested 2000–2008).
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who received traditional training under Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White (born 1953) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He received his doctorate from the University of Chicago (~1981–1988) and held positions at Chicago (~1983–1986), the University of Virginia (~1986–1996), and UC Santa Barbara (~1996).

David J. Kalupahana (1936–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Ceylon and the University of London (PhD ~1963–1966), he held posts at Ceylon (~1959–1971) and the University of Hawaii (~1972–2014).

David Jones, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, received his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaii. By 2007, he served as a professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and directed the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt (1937–2006) was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell (PhD ~1960–1966). He held academic posts at SOAS (~1962–1968), the University of Michigan (~1968–1969), and Cornell University (~1969–2002).
David Kerman Tomlinson specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019) and held a post at Smith College.

David Kinsley (1939–2000) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (~1964–1970) before holding a post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.
David Kopf (1930–2023) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Chicago from ~1958 to ~1964 and held a post at the University of Minnesota from ~1967 to ~1998.

David L. Gosling (born 1939) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and had an affiliation with the University of Cambridge attested in 2001.
